outline: 1013 Angles in a Right Angle and Straight Line

examples.solution_text:
The three angles fill a right angle, so they add to $90^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}24+31+x&=90\\55+x&=90\\x&=90-55\\x&=35\end{aligned}$

The missing angle is $35^{\circ}$. Turning the diagram would not change the right-angle total.

The outside arms point in opposite directions. The three angles fill a half turn, so they add to $180^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}48+x+69&=180\\117+x&=180\\x&=180-117\\x&=63\end{aligned}$

The missing angle is $63^{\circ}$.

Include every sector around the vertex: together they make $360^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}80+95+110+x&=360\\285+x&=360\\x&=360-285\\x&=75\end{aligned}$

The missing angle is $75^{\circ}$.

The smaller angle and the reflex angle fill one complete turn.

$\begin{aligned}58+r&=360\\r&=360-58\\r&=302\end{aligned}$

The reflex angle is $302^{\circ}$.

examples.question_text:
Check each claim. Give a reason.

(a) Two angles filling a marked right angle are measured as $36^{\circ}$ and $49^{\circ}$.

(b) An angle and its reflex angle are measured as $83^{\circ}$ and $277^{\circ}$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $36+49=85$.

The measurements are incorrect: angles filling a right angle must add to $90^{\circ}$.

(b) $83+277=360$.

The measurements satisfy the relationship: the angle and its reflex angle fill a complete turn and add to $360^{\circ}$.
The claim is incorrect. The outside arms do not point in opposite directions, so the marked angles do not fill a straight angle. Sharing a vertex alone does not give a total of $180^{\circ}$.

examples.derivation: The marked sectors fill the right angle. 24+31=55; 90−55=35, so x=35°. Ray directions give sectors of 24°, 31° and 35°.
The opposite horizontal arms enclose a half turn. 48+69=117; 180−117=63, so x=63°. The middle sector spans 111°−48°=63°.
All four sectors partition the complete turn. 80+95+110=285; 360−285=75, so x=75°. The diagram's consecutive ray directions match each sector.
The 58° angle and the marked reflex sector complete one turn. 360−58=302, so r=302°. The reflex arc runs from 58° to 360°.
(a) 36+49=85°, which contradicts the stated right-angle total of 90°. (b) 83+277=360°, so the measurements satisfy the complete-turn relationship. These verbal checks need no additional diagram.
The selected sectors lie between outside arms directed at 25° and 180°, spanning 155°, not 180°. The arms are not opposite; sharing a vertex cannot establish a straight-angle total.
